REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 12, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR

AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Bruce W. Barrows.

 4.  Roll Call

  Community College President (Hispanic Heritage Month).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, announced that prior to the meeting the
  Council/Agency members received full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written
  comment submitted for meeting items by the deadline listed on the agenda and for
  inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted
  for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer.

  John Darnell expressed concern regarding lack of a Neighborhood Watch meeting
  location at Frontier Park due to the removal of the benches at the former picnic shelter
  area.

  Peter Park expressed concern regarding illegal dumping and damage done by a
  contractor performing work in the City.

  David Pylman expressed thanks to City staff for their assistance with the new City
  website, thanked the City Clerk for her service, and expressed concern with the
  Ticketmaster services at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Jerry Jenson expressed support for the improvement of the parking situation near the
  Gold’s Gym in Cerritos.

  Sam Desai thanked the City Clerk for her years of service to the City of Cerritos.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Written comments, if submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda, are considered
  part of the meeting record and are available upon request in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer during regular business hours.

6A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 2.15 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  EXTEND THE TWO-YEAR TERMS OF OFFICE FOR 2022-24 ADVISORY BOARD,
  COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed concern with the protocol for the development of new Advisory
  Boards, Commissions, and Commissions and the selection of their corresponding
  advisory board members.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama and seconded by Barrows to waive full reading of
  and introduce Ordinance No. 1047, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
  AMENDING CHAPTER 2.15 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE TO EXTEND THE
  TWO-YEAR TERMS OF OFFICE FOR 2022-24 ADVISORY BOARD, COMMISSION,
  AND COMMITTEE MEMBERS (COUNCIL), containing the modifications to the Cerritos
  Municipal Code chapter 2.15 with deletions in strikeout text and additions in bold
  italics text:

  Chapter 2.15 - Advisory Boards, Commissions, and Committees Section

  2.15.010 Terms of Office

  (a) All City Council appointments to City of Cerritos Advisory Boards, Commissions,
  and Committees shall be for a term of two years commencing on the 1st day of the
  month after the Annual Mayoral Transition conducted in even odd-numbered years
  to coincide with the City's General Municipal Election cycle; or shall expire earlier if
  the Councilmember making the appointment ceases to hold office as a member of
  the Cerritos City Council. Persons appointed may be removed by action of the
  Councilmember making the appointment, subject to approval by the City Council or
  by a majority vote of the City Council. Appointments may be extended pursuant to
  subsection (b) of this section;

  (b) The term of any regular member of any City of Cerritos Advisory Board,
  Commission, or Committee is automatically extended for not more than ninety days
  pending the qualification of his or her successor;

  (c) If a vacancy shall occur otherwise than by expiration of term, it shall be filled by
  appointment for the unexpired portion of the term. Such appointment shall be made
  by the Councilmember making the original appointment, with the approval of the
  City Council; and

  (d) Notwithstanding subsection (b) of this section, for members serving the 2022-
  2024 term only, the term of any regular member of any City of Cerritos Advisory
  Board, Commission, or Committee is automatically extended for not more than one
  hundred eighty days through and including the last day of the month in which
  the Mayor is selected pursuant to Section 404 of the Cerritos City Charter as
  part of the 2025 annual Mayoral Transition, pending the qualification of his or
  her successor
